findings.summary: The site does not provide a user-preference-driven dark theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the normal capture, while the reduced-motion computed probe reports body background rgb(255,255,255) and color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and adapt surfaces, text, controls, and browser chrome through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Search state and panel changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The search CSS/DOM probe found no view-transition declarations despite pagination, filters, save panels, and result-state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document View Transitions to meaningful filter, pagination, and panel state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Numerous overlays and action panels use custom controls instead of native dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The search probe found 0 dialog, 0 popover, and 0 details elements while the DOM exposes Save, Email, Send to, citation, RSS, and filter panels with custom trigger/cancel wiring.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient menus to popover and modal tasks to dialog, retaining explicit accessible names and native light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Responsive layouts rely on viewport rules rather than component-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: The live stylesheet probe found no @container rules. Mobile screenshots show a good viewport adaptation, but reusable result, search, and builder components have no container-query behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type and targeted @container rules for reusable search/result and builder components where they appear in different widths.

findings.summary: Throttled mobile LCP is above the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.0 s and FCP 2.3 s. A separate trace was faster at LCP 1.54 s, so the slower mobile condition is the actionable case; CLS remained 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content and shorten critical resource chains while preserving the observed zero CLS.

findings.summary: Five stylesheets and synchronous scripts create avoidable critical-path work.
findings.evidence: HAR identified five parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets; the DOM confirmed several parser scripts lack async/defer, and Lighthouse estimated 990 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate or split critical CSS, defer non-critical CSS, and defer or conditionally load scripts that are not required for initial results.

findings.summary: The result page ships substantial unused and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 303 KiB unused JavaScript and 39 KiB legacy JavaScript; HAR measured 799,880 transferred script bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to split page-specific bundles and conditionally load analytics, survey, export, and panel code only when needed.

findings.summary: Some images do not reserve explicit dimensions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the explicit width/height image audit, although the layout observer measured CLS 0 in this run.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width and height or aspect-ratio for every content image and icon represented by img.

findings.guidanceId: structured data schema.org json-ld open graph social preview metadata
findings.summary: Article pages provide social metadata but no structured scholarly-article data.
findings.evidence: The raw 200 article HTML has descriptive title, description, canonical, and Open Graph tags, but contains zero application/ld+json blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate ScholarlyArticle or MedicalScholarlyArticle JSON-LD matching the visible citation, authors, journal, date, identifiers, and abstract.

findings.summary: Transport is strong, but CSP is absent and an analytics cookie is set without Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no Content-Security-Policy. Cookie evidence found _ga_DP2X732JSX with secure=false and a 400-day lifetime. HSTS, nosniff, DENY framing, and same-origin referrer policy were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP in report-only mode then enforce it; ensure every analytics cookie is Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite and lifetime.

findings.summary: Analytics and survey dependencies dominate the transferred page weight.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 43 third-party requests and 942,337 third-party bytes, including 446,606 bytes from Google Tag Manager and 106,887 from Qualtrics; trackers detected GTM and Google Analytics.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize measurement to essential events, consolidate tags, load surveys only after contextual eligibility, and require a documented retention and consent basis.

findings.summary: The response omits Permissions-Policy and CSP-based defenses.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no Permissions-Policy and no CSP. HSTS and X-Frame-Options: DENY are correctly present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive Permissions-Policy and include frame-ancestors plus suitable Trusted Types policy in CSP where compatible.

findings.summary: The globally used interface declares English but does not use CSS logical properties in the inspected search bundle.
findings.evidence: The probe found html lang=en, but no margin-inline or padding-inline and no dir declaration; this makes future bidirectional/localized layouts more costly.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inline/block properties and verify representative pages under dir=rtl; retain accurate language declarations.

findings.summary: Background analytics and survey code adds substantial work unrelated to the immediate literature task.
findings.evidence: The load made 43 third-party requests; GTM, federal analytics, Google Analytics, and Qualtrics scripts together account for most of the 978,202 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential analytics and surveys until idle or contextual interaction, batch events, and remove duplicate trackers.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript is disproportionate for a text-first search result page.
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 942,337 of 978,202 bytes (96%); scripts alone transferred 799,880 bytes while the page contains primarily text citations.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove duplicate tag-manager payloads, and lazy-load Qualtrics only when a survey is shown.

findings.summary: Machine-readable content is strong, but task capabilities are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: Discoverability found 100% raw-HTML coverage on the home page, but probes found no agent-tool registration or structured capability surface for search, filters, citation export, or save actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat this as an emerging opportunity: expose safe search, citation retrieval, and export actions through structured agent-facing tools with clear confirmation boundaries.

taskList.title: Minimize, consolidate, and defer analytics, tag-manager, and Qualtrics dependencies; set a third-party byte/request budget.
Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, restrictive Permissions-Policy, and secure, narrowly scoped analytics cookies.
Shorten critical CSS/script chains and split unused/legacy JavaScript from initial search results.
Replace custom transient panels with native popover and modal tasks with dialog.
Add a preference-driven dark color scheme across every surface and control.
Add accurate ScholarlyArticle structured data to article details.
